stem: The most basic natural unit of time, based on one rotation of the Earth, is the __________.
solution: A day corresponds to one rotation of the Earth about its axis.

stem: Day and night are caused by the __________ of the Earth on its axis.
solution: The Earth's rotation brings different parts into and out of sunlight, causing day and night.

stem: The natural unit of time based on the phases of the Moon is the __________.
solution: A month is based on the cycle of the Moon's phases (a lunar month).

stem: The natural unit of time based on one revolution of the Earth around the Sun is the __________.
solution: A year corresponds to one revolution of the Earth around the Sun.

stem: The changing shapes of the Moon over a month are called the __________ of the Moon.
solution: The phases of the Moon are the different lit shapes seen through a lunar month.

stem: One complete cycle of the Moon's phases takes about __________.
solution: The Moon's phase cycle repeats in roughly a month.

stem: A device that uses the shadow of a rod cast by the Sun to tell time is a __________.
solution: A sundial tells time from the position of the shadow cast by the Sun.

stem: A limitation of a sundial is that it cannot be used __________.
options: at night or on a cloudy day
solution: A sundial needs sunlight, so it fails at night and when it is cloudy.

stem: Early people measured short intervals of time using a __________, in which water drips at a steady rate.
solution: A water clock measures time by the steady flow of water.

stem: A sand clock (hourglass) measures time by the flow of __________.
solution: In a sand clock, sand trickles through a narrow neck at a steady rate to mark time.

stem: The regular to-and-fro motion of a pendulum is called __________.
solution: The back-and-forth swing of a pendulum is an oscillation.

stem: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one full oscillation is called its __________.
solution: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation of the pendulum.

stem: For a simple pendulum, the time period depends mainly on the __________ of the pendulum.
solution: The time period of a simple pendulum depends chiefly on its length.

stem: A longer pendulum has a __________ time period.
solution: The longer the pendulum, the longer the time it takes for one oscillation.

stem: Pendulum clocks keep good time because the pendulum's oscillations are __________.
options: regular and of fixed time period
solution: A pendulum swings with a fixed, regular time period, allowing accurate timekeeping.

stem: The number of oscillations made in one second is called the __________.
solution: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second.

stem: Modern wristwatches and clocks keep accurate time using vibrations of a __________ crystal.
solution: Quartz crystals vibrate at a very steady rate, making quartz clocks accurate.

stem: The most accurate clocks used as time standards today are __________ clocks.
solution: Atomic clocks are the most precise, based on the vibrations of atoms.

stem: The SI unit of time is the __________.
solution: The second is the SI unit of time.

stem: There are __________ seconds in one minute.
solution: One minute contains 60 seconds.

stem: There are __________ hours in one day.
solution: A day has 24 hours.

stem: Ancient calendars were based on the movements of the __________.
solution: Calendars were developed by observing the regular movements of the Sun and Moon.

stem: A calendar based mainly on the phases of the Moon is called a __________ calendar.
solution: A lunar calendar is based on the Moon's phases.

stem: A calendar based mainly on the Earth's revolution around the Sun is called a __________ calendar.
solution: A solar calendar is based on the year defined by Earth's revolution around the Sun.

stem: An extra day is added in a leap year because the actual year is about __________.
solution: A year is about 365¼ days, so an extra day is added every four years (leap year).

stem: The seasons repeat every year because of the tilt of the Earth's axis and its __________.
solution: The tilt combined with Earth's yearly revolution produces the repeating cycle of seasons.

stem: The apparent movement of the Sun across the sky from east to west is due to the Earth's __________.
solution: The Earth's west-to-east rotation makes the Sun appear to move east to west.

stem: The shadow of a stick in sunlight is shortest around __________.
solution: Near noon the Sun is highest, so the shadow of a vertical stick is shortest.

stem: A shadow clock works on the principle that the shadow of an object __________ during the day.
solution: As the Sun moves, the shadow's length and direction change, indicating the time.

stem: The main advantage of mechanical and electronic clocks over natural time markers is that they __________.
options: work at all times, day or night
solution: Mechanical and electronic clocks run continuously, unlike sundials that need sunlight.

stem: The amplitude of a pendulum is the __________ of its swing from the central position.
solution: Amplitude is the greatest distance the pendulum bob moves from its rest position.

stem: If a pendulum makes 20 oscillations in 40 seconds, its time period is __________.
solution: Time period = total time / number of oscillations = 40 / 20 = 2 seconds.

stem: The Moon takes about the same time to rotate once as to revolve once around the Earth, so we always see __________.
options: the same side of the Moon
solution: Because its rotation and revolution periods match, the Moon always shows us the same face.

stem: The regular rising and setting of the Sun gives us a natural measure of the __________.
solution: Sunrise and sunset mark the natural cycle of a day.

stem: The 'week' as a unit of time is __________.
options: a human-made grouping of days, not a natural cycle
solution: Unlike the day, month and year, the week is a convenient human invention, not a natural astronomical cycle.

stem: A stopwatch is used to measure __________ time intervals accurately.
solution: A stopwatch is designed to measure short intervals of time precisely.

stem: Timekeeping is important in daily life because it helps us to __________.
solution: Accurate time lets people schedule and coordinate their activities.

stem: The regularity of the Earth's rotation makes the length of a day __________.
solution: The Earth's steady rotation keeps the length of a day nearly the same, useful for timekeeping.

stem: Galileo is associated with the study of the __________ that led to accurate clocks.
solution: Galileo studied the regular swinging of the pendulum, which later led to pendulum clocks.

stem: The direction of the shadow of a vertical stick at sunrise points roughly towards the __________.
solution: At sunrise the Sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west.

stem: A quartz clock is more accurate than a pendulum clock mainly because quartz vibrations are __________.
solution: Quartz crystals vibrate very rapidly and regularly, giving greater accuracy.

stem: The seasons and the calendar are ultimately linked to the motion of the __________.
solution: The year, seasons and solar calendar all come from the Earth's revolution around the Sun.

stem: An eclipse is a relatively __________ event compared with the daily rising of the Sun.
solution: Eclipses occur only occasionally, unlike the everyday cycle of day and night.

stem: The key idea of this chapter is that regular __________ events have long been used to measure time.
solution: Regular movements in the sky — day, month, year — have always been used to keep time.

stem: The advantage of a natural time unit like the day is that it is __________.
solution: The day is easy to observe and regular, making it a natural unit of time.

stem: A pendulum's time period does NOT depend on the __________.
solution: For a simple pendulum, the time period does not depend on the mass of the bob.

stem: The Sun crossing the local sky at its highest point marks local __________.
solution: When the Sun is highest in the sky, it is local noon.

stem: The main reason different time-measuring devices were invented over history was the need for __________.
solution: People invented better clocks to measure time more accurately and conveniently.

stem: One oscillation of a pendulum means the bob moves __________.
options: from one extreme to the other and back
solution: One oscillation is a complete to-and-fro swing back to the starting point.

stem: The most reliable long-term marker for making a yearly calendar is the __________.
solution: The Sun's yearly cycle (the Earth's revolution) is the reliable basis for a yearly calendar.
